claim: BK channels are regulated by cytosolic Ca2+ and depolarizing voltages.
source: Since the BK channels are regulated by cytosolic Ca2+ and depolarizing voltages (Marty, 1981; Pallotta et al., 1981; Latorre et al., 1982), they are integrators of physiological stimuli involving intracellular Ca2+ elevation and membrane excitability.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to three published studies (Marty, 1981; Pallotta et al., 1981; Latorre et al., 1982).

claim: BK channels are integrators of physiological stimuli involving intracellular Ca2+ elevation and membrane excitability.
source: Since the BK channels are regulated by cytosolic Ca2+ and depolarizing voltages (Marty, 1981; Pallotta et al., 1981; Latorre et al., 1982), they are integrators of physiological stimuli involving intracellular Ca2+ elevation and membrane excitability.
evidence: This is inferred from the dual regulation by Ca2+ and voltage, supported by citations.

claim: Functional BK channels are formed by homotetramers of α-subunits.
source: Functional BK channels are formed by homotetramers of α-subunits (Shen et al., 1994)
evidence: Supported by citation to Shen et al., 1994.

claim: Each BK α-subunit comprises a transmembrane voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and an intracellular Ca2+-sensing C-terminal domain (CTD).
source: each comprising a transmembrane voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and an intracellular Ca2+-sensing C-terminal domain (CTD) that can independently modulate the ion conduction gate in the pore domain (PD) (Latorre et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Latorre et al., 2017.

claim: The VSD and CTD can independently modulate the ion conduction gate in the pore domain.
source: each comprising a transmembrane voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and an intracellular Ca2+-sensing C-terminal domain (CTD) that can independently modulate the ion conduction gate in the pore domain (PD) (Latorre et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Latorre et al., 2017.

claim: The CTDs consist of two non-identical regulators of the conductance of K+ domains (RCK1 and RCK2) arranged in a ring-like tetrameric structure dubbed the gating ring.
source: The CTDs consist of two non-identical regulators of the conductance of K+ domains (RCK1 and RCK2) arranged in a ring-like tetrameric structure dubbed the gating ring (Wu et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2012; Hite et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to structural studies.

claim: Each RCK domain contains distinct ligand-binding sites capable of detecting Ca2+ in the micromolar range.
source: Each RCK domain contains distinct ligand-binding sites capable of detecting Ca2+ in the micromolar range (Schreiber and Salkoff, 1997; Bao et al., 2002; Xia et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: In the absence of Ca2+, very positive membrane potentials are required to drive all voltage sensors to their active conformations.
source: With 0 Ca2+, very positive membrane potentials are required to drive all voltage sensors to their active conformations (Cui et al., 1997; Stefani et al., 1997; Horrigan et al., 1999; Contreras et al., 2012)
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: An appreciable open probability of BK channels at physiologically relevant voltages requires the activation of the Ca2+ sensors on the gating ring.
source: Thus, in cells such as neurons, an appreciable open probability of BK channels at physiologically relevant voltages necessarily requires the activation of the Ca2+ sensors on the gating ring.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement of very positive voltages in the absence of Ca2+ and established knowledge about physiological voltage ranges.

claim: The RCK1 site occupancy is voltage-dependent.
source: The voltage dependence of Ca2+-dependent gating ring rearrangements (Miranda et al., 2013; Miranda et al., 2018) and RCK1 site occupancy (Sweet and Cox, 2008; Savalli et al., 2012; Miranda et al., 2018)
evidence: Supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: VSD movements are perturbed by Ca2+ binding.
source: as well as the perturbation of VSD movements by Ca2+ binding (Savalli et al., 2012)
evidence: Supported by citation to Savalli et al., 2012.

claim: The physical CTD-VSD interface provides the structure capable of mediating the crosstalk between these sensory modules.
source: The physical CTD-VSD interface has been suggested to provide the structure capable of mediating the crosstalk between these sensory modules and their synergy in activating the pore domain (Yang et al., 2007; Sun et al., 2013; Tao et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural and functional studies.

claim: The RCK1 and RCK2 Ca2+-binding sites have distinct functional properties.
source: The RCK1 and RCK2 Ca2+-binding sites have distinct functional properties conferred by their different molecular structures and relative positions within the gating ring (Wu et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2012; Hite et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: The RCK sites differ in their Ca2+ binding affinities.
source: Thus, the RCK sites differ in their Ca2+ binding affinities (Bao et al., 2002; Xia et al., 2002; Sweet and Cox, 2008)
evidence: Supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: The RCK sites differ in their divalent cations selectivity.
source: divalent cations selectivity (Oberhauser et al., 1988; Schreiber and Salkoff, 1997; Zeng et al., 2005; Zhou et al., 2012)
evidence: Supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The RCK sites differ in their voltage dependence.
source: voltage dependence (Sweet and Cox, 2008; Savalli et al., 2012; Miranda et al., 2018)
evidence: Supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The RCK sites differ in their contribution to allosteric gating mechanisms.
source: and in their contribution to allosteric gating mechanisms (Yang et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: Only the RCK1 site appears to be involved in communicating the Ca2+-dependent conformational changes towards the membrane-spanning VSD.
source: In particular, only the RCK1 site appears to be involved in communicating the Ca2+-dependent conformational changes towards the membrane-spanning VSD (Savalli et al., 2012; Miranda et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The Aplysia BK structure reveals that the N-lobe of the RCK1 domain is in non-covalent contact with the VSD and the S4-S5 linker.
source: Recently, the Aplysia BK structure has revealed that the N-lobe of the RCK1 domain is in a non-covalent contact with the VSD and the S4-S5 linker that connects the voltage sensor to the pore domain.
evidence: Based on structural data from Aplysia BK channel.

claim: The RCK1-VSD interaction surface is rearranged when comparing the liganded and Ca2+-free structures.
source: This RCK1-VSD interaction surface is rearranged when comparing the liganded and Ca2+-free structures (Hite et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Ca2+-induced rearrangements of the gating ring should be transmitted to the pore domain via the VSD.
source: In fact, it has been hypothesized that any Ca2+-induced rearrangements of the gating ring should ultimately be transmitted to the pore domain via the VSD (Hite et al., 2017; Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Ca2+ sensor occupancy has a strong impact on VSD activation through a coordinated interaction mechanism in which Ca2+ binding to a single α-subunit affects all VSDs equally.
source: Our results indicate that Ca2+ sensor occupancy has a strong impact on VSD activation through a coordinated interaction mechanism in which Ca2+ binding to a single α-subunit affects all VSDs equally.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The two distinct high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites contained in the C-terminus domains, RCK1 and RCK2, contribute equally to decrease the free energy necessary to activate the VSD.
source: Moreover, the two distinct high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites contained in the C-terminus domains, RCK1 and RCK2, contribute equally to decrease the free energy necessary to activate the VSD.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Voltage-dependent gating and pore opening in BK channels is modulated to a great extent by the interaction between Ca2+ sensors and VSDs.
source: We conclude that voltage-dependent gating and pore opening in BK channels is modulated to a great extent by the interaction between Ca2+ sensors and VSDs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The fast ON-gating current relaxation exhibits an almost complete decay before the IK achieves an exponential time course in 0 Ca2+ conditions.
source: The IG-ON relaxation exhibits an almost complete decay before the IK achieves an exponential time course in 0 Ca2+ conditions (Figure 1A).
evidence: This observation is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The time constant of the IK activation is ~3.4 ms at 160 mV in 0 Ca2+ conditions.
source: Thus, the time constant of the IK activation (~3.4 ms at 160 mV) following a delay of ~160 µs is consistent with the movement of the voltage sensors preceding channel opening.
evidence: This is a measurement from experimental data.

claim: Under saturating internal Ca2+ conditions, the IG-ON time course develops 20 times faster than the exponential kinetic of the IK activation.
source: Under saturating internal Ca2+ conditions, the IG-ON time course develops 20 times faster than the exponential kinetic of the IK activation (τIG−ON  = 30 µs and ΔtIK = 660 µs at 160 mV)
evidence: This is a measurement from experimental data.

claim: The fast IG-ON relaxation reflects the movement of the gating charge in the channel's closed conformation, regardless of internal Ca2+ concentration.
source: Thus, the fast IG-ON relaxation reflects the movement of the gating charge in the channel's closed conformation, regardless of internal Ca2+ concentration.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations that IG-ON completes before channel opening at both 0 and 100 µM Ca2+.

claim: Increasing the Ca2+ concentration promoted a large leftward shift (∆VH = -142.6 ± 4.5 mV) of the normalized QC curves.
source: Increasing the Ca2+ concentration promoted a large leftward shift (∆VH = -142.6 ± 4.5 mV) of the normalized QC (QC(V)/QC, MAX curves) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The predominant effect of Ca2+-binding on VSD activation causes a decrease in the backward rate constant at zero voltage (β0) from 76 ms−1 at 0 Ca2+ to 7 ms−1 at 100 μM Ca2+.
source: The predominant effect of Ca2+-binding on VSD activation appears to cause a decrease in the backward rate constant at zero voltage (β0; see Materials and methods). β0 decreases from 76 ms−1 at 0 Ca2+ to 7 ms−1 at 100 μM Ca2+
evidence: This is derived from fitting experimental data to a two-state model.

claim: Ca2+ binding to the RCK Ca2+-binding sites alters the VSD equilibrium, causing a decrease in the free energy (ΔΔGVCa) by ~8 kJ/mol (ΔΔGVCa= -7.98 ± 0.27 kJ/mol).
source: Such a large shift (ΔVH = -142.6 ± 4.5 mV) implies that Ca2+ binding to the RCK Ca2+-binding sites alters the VSD equilibrium, which in consequence causes a decrease in the free energy (ΔΔGVCa) that defines the voltage sensor R-A equilibrium (J) by ~8 kJ/mol (ΔΔGVCa= -7.98 ± 0.27 kJ/mol).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental measurements of voltage shifts.

claim: The J equilibrium constant of VSD becomes amplified by an allosteric factor E equal to 26.4 at Ca2+-saturated conditions.
source: In terms of the allosteric gating scheme (Horrigan and Aldrich, 2002), this result means that the J equilibrium constant of VSD becomes amplified by an allosteric factor E equal to 26.4 at Ca2+-saturated conditions (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The increase in internal Ca2+ promoted a leftward shift of the QC versus voltage curves.
source: The increase in internal Ca2+ promoted a leftward shift of the QC versus voltage (QC(V)) curves (Figure 2B-C), which indicates that Ca2+-binding facilitates the activation of the voltage sensor
evidence: This is observed in experimental data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: Ca2+-binding facilitates the activation of the voltage sensor, being more prominent as Ca2+-binding site occupancy increases.
source: The increase in internal Ca2+ promoted a leftward shift of the QC versus voltage (QC(V)) curves (Figure 2B-C), which indicates that Ca2+-binding facilitates the activation of the voltage sensor, being more prominent as Ca2+-binding site occupancy increases.
evidence: This is inferred from the dose-dependent leftward shift observed in experimental data.

claim: The OFF-gating current was dramatically modified becoming smaller in amplitude and with slower kinetics as the internal Ca2+ concentration was increased.
source: Figure 2A shows that the OFF-gating current was dramatically modified becoming smaller in amplitude and with slower kinetics as the internal Ca2+ concentration was increased
evidence: This is observed in experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At least two components (fast and slow components) could be resolved in the OFF gating current decay in 'zero' and 10 µM internal Ca2+ conditions.
source: At least two components (fast and slow components) could be resolved in the OFF gating current decay in 'zero' and 10 µM internal Ca2+ conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C).
evidence: This is observed in experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: The change in the time constant of the fast component of OFF-gating current at 10 µM Ca2+ relative to 'zero' Ca2+ condition agrees with a Ca2+-induced effect primarily on the backward rate of the R-A transition (β0 decreases from 76 ms−1 at 0 Ca2+ to 10.6 ms−1 at 10 μM Ca2+).
source: The change in the time constant of the fast component of OFF-gating current detected at 10 µM Ca2+ relative to 'zero' Ca2+ condition agrees with a Ca2+-induced effect primarily on the backward rate of the R-A transition (β0 decreases from 76 ms−1 at 0 Ca2+ to 10.6 ms−1 at 10 μM Ca2+, see Figure 2—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: This is derived from fitting experimental data to a two-state model.

claim: The relative contribution of the slower component increases as internal Ca2+ is increased, reflecting an increase in the open probability of the channel.
source: On the other hand, the relative contribution of the slower component increasing as internal Ca2+ is increased, reflecting an increase in the open probability of the channel (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E-F).
evidence: This is observed in experimental data and inferred to reflect channel opening.

claim: At -150 mV and -200 mV with 100 µM internal Ca2+, the charge displaced in the ON is recovered in the OFF.
source: At these applied voltages, the charge displaced in the ON is recovered in the OFF (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is observed in experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Scheme I proposes that Ca2+ binding to one α-subunit only affects the VSD in the same subunit.
source: The first mechanism proposes that Ca2+ binding to one α-subunit only affects the VSD in the same subunit (Scheme I) (Figure 3A)
evidence: This is a model proposed by Horrigan and Aldrich (2002) as cited in the text.

claim: Scheme II proposes that the Ca2+ binding affects all four VSD equally.
source: whereas the second mechanism proposes that the Ca2+ binding affects all four VSD equally (Scheme II) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a model proposed by Horrigan and Aldrich (2002) as cited in the text.

claim: The standard HA model assumes Scheme I as the Ca2+ binding-VSD interaction scheme underlying the general gating mechanism of BK channel.
source: Second, the model assumes the Scheme I as the Ca2+ binding-VSD interaction scheme underlying the general gating mechanism of BK channel (Horrigan and Aldrich, 2002).
evidence: This is stated as an assumption of the Horrigan-Aldrich model.

claim: At extreme conditions of low (0.03 to 0.1 µM) and high (≥100 µM) internal Ca2+, VSD activation behaves in a mechanism-independent manner since all voltage sensors are in the same functional state.
source: At extreme conditions of low (0.03 to 0.1 µM) and high (≥100 µM) internal Ca2+, VSD activation behaves in a mechanism-independent manner since all voltage sensors are in the same functional state (unliganded or saturated).
evidence: This is inferred from the properties of the two models at extreme Ca2+ concentrations.

claim: Scheme I predicts two functional states of the VSD depending on the occupancy status of the Ca2+ site (Ca2+ bound and unbound) such that the QC(V) curve is described by the fractional distribution of the unliganded and Ca2+-saturated functional states like an all-or-none allosteric effect.
source: Indeed, Scheme I predicts two functional states of the VSD depending on the occupancy status of the Ca2+ site (Ca2+ bound and unbound) such that the QC(V) curve is described by the fractional distribution of the unliganded and Ca2+-saturated functional states like an all-or-none allosteric effect (Figure 3C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Equation 4 in Appendix).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model (Scheme I).

claim: The Ca2+-binding effect on the VSD activation according to Scheme II is characterized by a five-component Boltzmann function.
source: By contrast, the Ca2+-binding effect on the VSD activation according to Scheme II is characterized by a five-component Boltzmann function (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Equation 6 in Appendix).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model (Scheme II).

claim: The experimental leftward shift of the QC(V) curves occur with constant slope (zQ), which is consistent with Model II.
source: The experimental leftward shift of the QC(V) curves occur with constant slope (zQ) (Figure 2B), which is consistent with Model II.
evidence: This is observed in experimental data and compared to model predictions.

claim: To recover the experimental zQ using Scheme I requires a Ca2+ binding rate constant that is 100-fold faster than the one reported by Hou et al. (2016) exceeding the diffusion limit constraint.
source: However, Figure 3—figure supplement 2 demonstrates that to recover the experimental zQ requires a Ca2+ binding rate constant that is 100-fold faster than the one reported by Hou et al. (2016) exceeding the diffusion limit constraint.
evidence: This is demonstrated through modeling shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ca2+-binding is slow enough to safely ignore calcium re-equilibration during the 100 μs it takes to measure the gating charges.
source: Therefore, we can conclude that Ca2+-binding is slow enough to safely ignore calcium re-equilibration during the 100 μs it takes to measure the gating charges.
evidence: This is concluded from the analysis of Ca2+ binding kinetics relative to VSD activation kinetics.

claim: Based on the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), the model that fits to the QC(V,Ca2+) data best is Model II.
source: Based on the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) (Akaike, 1974), the model that fits to the QC(V,Ca2+) data best is Model II, whereas the probability of the Model I being the best model is negligible (wi = 10−47) (Table 1).
evidence: This is determined by statistical analysis (AIC) of model fits to experimental data.

claim: The probability of Model I being the best model is negligible (wi = 10−47).
source: Based on the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) (Akaike, 1974), the model that fits to the QC(V,Ca2+) data best is Model II, whereas the probability of the Model I being the best model is negligible (wi = 10−47) (Table 1).
evidence: This is determined by statistical analysis (AIC) of model fits to experimental data.

claim: Model I predicts a pronounced decrease in the zQ parameter of the QC(V) curves at intermediate Ca2+ conditions which differs markedly from the experimental values.
source: However, Model I predicts a pronounced decrease in the zQ parameter of the QC(V) curves at intermediate Ca2+ conditions which differs markedly from the experimental values (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is shown by comparing model predictions to experimental data in Figure 4D.

claim: The behavior of QC(V) curves at intermediate Ca2+ concentrations (1-10 µM) is qualitatively consistent with the phenotype exhibited by the Ca2+-VSD scheme II.
source: Additionally, the behavior of QC(V) curves at intermediate Ca2+ concentrations (1-10 µM) is qualitatively consistent with the phenotype exhibited by the Ca2+-VSD scheme II (Figure 3D and Figure 4B).
evidence: This is observed by comparing experimental data to model predictions.

claim: The experimental dose-dependent effect of Ca2+ on voltage sensor activation suggests that Ca2+-binding to a single α-subunit of BK channels increases E-fold the equilibrium constant J of all four voltage sensors.
source: Thus, the experimental dose-dependent effect of Ca2+ on voltage sensor activation suggests that Ca2+-binding to a single α-subunit of BK channels increases E-fold the equilibrium constant J that defines the equilibrium between resting and active conformations of the voltage sensors in all four subunits.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental data and model fitting results.

claim: Under physiological conditions, the RCK1 and RCK2 high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites are responsible for all the calcium sensitivity of the activation of BK channel.
source: Under physiological conditions, the RCK1 and RCK2 high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites are responsible for all the calcium sensitivity of the activation of BK channel (Schreiber and Salkoff, 1997; Bao et al., 2002; Bao et al., 2004; Xia et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: Disruption of the RCK1 Ca2+-sensor by the double mutant D362A/D367A significantly reduced (48%, ΔVH(D362A/D367A) = -74.9 ± 4.7 mV) the leftward shift of the QC(V) curves at 100 μM Ca2+ compared with that for the wild-type BK channel.
source: Disruption of the RCK1 Ca2+-sensor by the double mutant D362A/D367A (Xia et al., 2002) significantly reduced (48%, ΔVH(D362A/D367A) = -74.9 ± 4.7 mV) the leftward shift of the QC(V) curves at 100 μM Ca2+ compared with that for the wild-type (WT) BK channel (Figure 5A, C).
evidence: This is measured from experimental data shown in Figure 5A, C.

claim: The mutant M513I eliminates the Ca2+ sensitivity mediated by the RCK1 site.
source: We also examined the effect of the mutant M513I (Bao et al., 2002) which has been shown to eliminate the Ca2+ sensitivity mediated by the RCK1 site (Bao et al., 2002; Bao et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: In the M513I mutant, the 100 µM Ca2+-induced shift in VH of the VSD activation curve was considerably smaller compared to that for the WT channel (about 54%, ΔVH(M513I) = -65.4 ± 2.6 mV).
source: In this mutant, the 100 µM Ca2+-induced shift in VH of the VSD activation curve was also considerably smaller compared to that for the WT channel (about 54%, ΔVH(M513I) = -65.4 ± 2.6 mV) (Figure 6).
evidence: This is measured from experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Both D362A/D367A and M513I mutations affect the Ca2+-induced enhancement of the activation of the voltage sensor very similarly through the RCK1 site.
source: Therefore, both mutations affect the Ca2+-induced enhancement of the activation of the voltage sensor very similarly through the RCK1 site (Figure 6C)
evidence: This is concluded from comparing experimental data for both mutants.

claim: The M513 residue appears to participate in the stabilization of the proper conformation of the RCK1 Ca2+-site.
source: The M513 residue appears to participate in the stabilization of the proper conformation of the RCK1 Ca2+-site whereas D367 is a key residue in the coordination of Ca2+ ions (Wu et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2010; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural and functional studies.

claim: D367 is a key residue in the coordination of Ca2+ ions.
source: The M513 residue appears to participate in the stabilization of the proper conformation of the RCK1 Ca2+-site whereas D367 is a key residue in the coordination of Ca2+ ions (Wu et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2010; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Neutralization of the residues forming part of the Ca2+ bowl (5D5A mutant) on the RCK2 domain decreased the leftward shift of the QC(V) curve by approximately 54% (ΔVH(5D5A) = -65.7 ± 4.7 mV) when Ca2+ was increased up to 100 μM.
source: On the other hand, neutralization of the residues forming part of the Ca2+ bowl (Schreiber and Salkoff, 1997) (5D5A mutant, see Materials and methods) on the RCK2 domain decreased the leftward shift of the QC(V) curve by approximately 54% (ΔVH(5D5A) = -65.7 ± 4.7 mV) when Ca2+ was increased up to 100 μM (Figure 5B, D).
evidence: This is measured from experimental data shown in Figure 5B, D.

claim: The effect of Ca2+ binding on ∆VH contributed by each high-affinity Ca2+ site is roughly half that for WT channels with both sites intact.
source: The effect of Ca2+ binding on ∆VH contributed by each high-affinity Ca2+ site is roughly half that for WT channels with both sites intact (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is observed by comparing experimental data for mutants to WT channels in Figure 5E.

claim: Both high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites contribute approximately equally to the decrease in free energy that is necessary to activate the VSD.
source: Therefore, both high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites contribute approximately equally to the decrease in free energy that is necessary to activate the VSD.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental data showing similar effects of RCK1 and RCK2 site mutations.

claim: The change of free energy of the resting-active equilibrium of the voltage sensor in response to Ca2+-binding at RCK2 site is ~ -4 kJ/mol (ΔΔGVCa(D362A/D367A) = -4.2 ± 0.3 kJ/mol and ΔΔGVCa(M513I) = -3.6 ± 0.5 kJ/mol).
source: Indeed, the change of free energy of the resting-active equilibrium of the voltage sensor in response to Ca2+-binding at RCK2 site is ~ -4 kJ/mol (ΔΔGVCa(D362A/D367A) = -4.2 ± 0.3 kJ/mol and ΔΔGVCa(M513I) = -3.6 ± 0.5 kJ/mol) (Figure 5C and Figure 6C).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental measurements shown in Figure 5C and Figure 6C.

claim: The occupation of the RCK1 Ca2+-binding site decreased the free energy necessary to activate the VSD by -3.8 ± 0.4 kJ/mol (ΔΔGVCa(5D5A)).
source: Similarly, the occupation of the RCK1 Ca2+-binding site decreased the free energy necessary to activate the VSD in -3.8 ± 0.4 kJ/mol (ΔΔGVCa(5D5A)).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental measurements.

claim: These findings reveal an additive effect of Ca2+-binding to the RCK1 and Ca2+ bowl sites on the VSD activation, which suggest independent allosteric pathways through which they exert their modulation on the VSD.
source: Remarkably, these findings reveal an additive effect of Ca2+-binding to the RCK1 and Ca2+ bowl sites on the VSD activation, which suggest independent allosteric pathways through which they exert their modulation on the VSD.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observation that each site contributes approximately equally and independently.

claim: Ca2+-binding significantly facilitates VSD activation through direct energetic contribution to the R-A equilibrium (ΔVH = -142.6 ± 4.5 mV and ΔΔGVCa = -7.98 ± 0.27 kJ/mol).
source: Thus, by characterizing the voltage dependence of charge movement in the virtual absence of internal Ca2+ and at Ca2+ concentrations that saturate the Ca2+ high-affinity sites, this work directly establishes that Ca2+-binding significantly facilitates VSD activation through direct energetic contribution to the R-A equilibrium (ΔVH = -142.6 ± 4.5 mV and ΔΔGVCa = -7.98 ± 0.27 kJ/mol).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on experimental data.

claim: This result is in agreement with previous reports from our laboratory (ΔVH = -140 mV and ΔΔGVCa = -7.9 kJ/mol; at [Ca2+]i = 100 µM).
source: Although this result is in agreement with previous reports from our laboratory (ΔVH = -140 mV and ΔΔGVCa = -7.9 kJ/mol; at [Ca2+]i = 100 µM) (Carrasquel-Ursulaez et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a comparison to previously published data from the same laboratory.

claim: The result is at odds with the smaller leftward shift obtained by Horrigan and Aldrich (2002) at saturating Ca2+ concentration (ΔVH = -33 mV and ΔΔGVCa = -1.9 kJ/mol; at [Ca2+]i = 70 µM).
source: it is at odds with the smaller leftward shift obtained by Horrigan and Aldrich (2002) at saturating Ca2+ concentration (ΔVH = -33 mV and ΔΔGVCa = -1.9 kJ/mol; at [Ca2+]i = 70 µM).
evidence: This is a comparison to previously published data from another laboratory.

claim: mBK channels share a high degree of identity with hBKs (96%).
source: Since mBK channels share a high degree of identity with hBKs (96%), it seems unlikely that the differences in Ca2+ binding and voltage sensor coupling are due to different BK clones.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of sequence homology between mouse and human BK channels.

claim: A sudden rise in intracellular [Ca2+] caused by UV flash induced-photolysis of caged Ca2+ prompts a leftward shift in both conductance-voltage (GV) and fluorescence-voltage (FV) relationships.
source: A sudden rise in intracellular [Ca2+] caused by a UV flash induced-photolysis of caged Ca2+ prompts a leftward shift in both conductance-voltage (GV) and fluorescence-voltage (FV) relationships.
evidence: This is based on fluorescence studies cited in the discussion.

claim: Functional activation of the gating ring is propagated to the VSD, leading to structural perturbations of voltages sensors, thereby favoring its active conformation.
source: These results suggest that functional activation of the gating ring is propagated to the VSD, leading to structural perturbations of voltages sensors, thereby favoring its active conformation (Savalli et al., 2012).
evidence: This is inferred from fluorescence studies cited in the discussion.

claim: The structural rearrangement of the gating ring in response to Ca2+ has a voltage dependence attributable to the operation of the voltage sensor.
source: Second, the structural rearrangement of the gating ring in response to Ca2+ has a voltage dependence (Miranda et al., 2013; Miranda et al., 2018) attributable to the operation of the voltage sensor.
evidence: Supported by citations to fluorescence studies.

claim: Mutations of the charged residue on the S4 transmembrane segment (R210, R213, and E219) modify the conformational changes of the gating ring triggered by depolarization in correspondence to the observed GV shift measured for these channel constructs.
source: Both mutations of the charged residue on the S4 transmembrane segment (R210, R213, and E219) and the co-expression of the β1-subunit with BKα channel, modify the conformational changes of the gating ring triggered by depolarization in correspondence to the observed GV shift measured for these channel constructs.
evidence: Supported by citation to Miranda et al., 2018.

claim: Perturbations of pore opening equilibrium (e.g. through the F315A mutation or the assembly of BKα channel with γ1-subunit) does not modify the voltage-dependent reorganization of the gating ring.
source: In contrast, perturbations of pore opening equilibrium (e.g. through the F315A mutation or the assembly of BKα channel with γ1-subunit) does not modify the voltage-dependent reorganization of the gating ring (Miranda et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Miranda et al., 2018.

claim: In both MthK and BK channels the Ca2+-site occupancy triggers a conformational change corresponding to a symmetric overall rearrangement of the cytosolic tetrameric structure that is ultimately propagated to the transmembrane regions (TMD) via C-linker and in the BK channel, also via the protein-protein interfaces between the gating ring and the TMD.
source: In both MthK and BK channels the Ca2+-site occupancy triggers a conformational change corresponding to a symmetric overall rearrangement of the cytosolic tetrameric structure that is ultimately propagated to the transmembrane regions (TMD) via C-linker and in the BK channel, also via the protein-protein interfaces between the gating ring and the TMD (Jiang et al., 2002; Jiang et al., 2003; Ye et al., 2006; Yuan et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2012; Pau et al., 2011; Smith et al., 2012; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to structural studies.

claim: Each Ca2+-binding event produces a gradual conformational expansion of the gating ring affecting the four voltage sensors in each step through the progressive perturbations within the protein-protein interfaces.
source: Thus, we can speculate that each Ca2+-binding event produces a gradual conformational expansion of the gating ring affecting the four voltage sensors in each step through the progressive perturbations within the protein-protein interfaces.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on structural and functional data.

claim: The communication pathway through which the Ca2+-driven conformational changes are propagated to the voltage sensors appears to reside on the CTD-VSD interface that involves non-covalent interactions between RCK1 N-lobe and S0-S4 transmembrane segments.
source: As mentioned above, the communication pathway through which the Ca2+-driven conformational changes are propagated to the voltage sensors appears to reside on the CTD-VSD interface that involves non-covalent interactions between RCK1 N-lobe and S0-S4 transmembrane segments (Yang et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2008; Yang et al., 2010; Sun et al., 2013; Hite et al., 2017; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural and functional studies.

claim: The VSDs are domain-swapped with RCK domains in the gating ring.
source: we recall that the VSDs are domain-swapped with RCK domains in the gating ring (Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to structural study.

claim: Binding of Ca2+ makes the RCK1 N-lobe pull on the S6 helix from its subunit whereas the modification of the contact surface between the RCK1 N-lobe with the voltage sensor of an adjacent subunit induces an outward displacement of the voltage sensor.
source: Therefore, binding of Ca2+ makes the RCK1 N-lobe pull on the S6 helix from its subunit whereas the modification of the contact surface between the RCK1 N-lobe with the voltage sensor of an adjacent subunit induces an outward displacement of the voltage sensor (Hite et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to structural study.

claim: Residues on the βA-αC region are involved in the allosteric connection of the Ca2+-dependent activation mediated by RCK1 site occupancy.
source: Scanning mutagenesis of RCK1-N terminal subdomain indicates that residues on the βA-αC region are involved in the allosteric connection of the Ca2+-dependent activation mediated by RCK1 site occupancy (Yang et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to mutagenesis study.

claim: The selective activation of the RCK1 domain was identified as being responsible for the Ca2+-induced VSD rearrangement.
source: In line with this study, the selective activation of the RCK1 domain was identified as being responsible for the Ca2+-induced VSD rearrangement (Savalli et al., 2012)
evidence: Supported by citation to functional study.

claim: The selective activation of the RCK1 domain was identified as being responsible for the voltage dependence of the Ca2+-driven motions of gating ring.
source: and the voltage dependence of the Ca2+-driven motions of gating ring (Miranda et al., 2016; Miranda et al., 2018)
evidence: Supported by citations to fluorescence studies.

claim: CTD-VSD allosteric coupling is primarily determined by the RCK1 site.
source: suggesting that CTD-VSD allosteric coupling is primarily determined by the RCK1 site (Sweet and Cox, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to functional study.

claim: The constructs D362A/D367A and 5D5A selectively impair the Ca2+-sensitivity of the RCK1- and RCK2-sensors, respectively, by neutralizing the residues that are involved in contributing to Ca2+-coordination.
source: The constructs D362A/D367A and 5D5A (D894A-D898A) selectively impair the Ca2+-sensitivity of the RCK1- and RCK2-sensors, respectively, by neutralizing the residues that are involved in contributing to Ca2+-coordination (Zhang et al., 2010; Tao et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural and functional studies.

claim: The energetic effect of Ca2+-binding on voltage sensor equilibrium is practically identical (~ −4 kJ/mol) for both the D362A/D367A and the 5D5A mutations.
source: Comparing the fast gating charge movement at 0 Ca2+ and saturating Ca2+ conditions reveals that the energetic effect of Ca2+-binding on voltage sensor equilibrium is practically identical (~ −4 kJ/mol) for both the D362A/D367A and the 5D5A mutations (Figure 5).
evidence: This is measured from experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The findings establish that the RCK2-driven contribution to CTD-VSD energetic coupling is quite similar to the RCK1-driven contribution.
source: Thus, our findings establish that the RCK2-driven contribution to CTD-VSD energetic coupling is quite similar to the RCK1-driven contribution.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental data showing similar energetic contributions.

claim: Mutations in each RCK site shift the Ca2+-dependent GV by approximately one-half relative to the effect seen for WT channels.
source: These findings remind us of early reports showing that mutations in each RCK site shift the Ca2+-dependent GV by approximately one-half relative to the effect seen for WT channels (Bao et al., 2002; Xia et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: The two RCK-sensors contribute independently to the modulation on the VSD.
source: Thus, our results suggest that the two RCK-sensors contribute independently to the modulation on the VSD, although we cannot eliminate the possibility of some cooperativity between them.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing additive effects.

claim: There is some, albeit modest, cooperativity between the two high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites although its nature is still unclear.
source: Indeed, various lines of evidence indicate that there is some, albeit modest, cooperativity between the two high-affinity Ca2+-binding sites although its nature is still unclear (Qian et al., 2006; Savalli et al., 2012; Sweet and Cox, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: Intra and intersubunit structural connectivity supports the putative cooperative interactions between the Ca2+ sensors at the gating ring.
source: Intra and intersubunit structural connectivity supports the putative cooperative interactions between the Ca2+ sensors at the gating ring (Hite et al., 2017; Yuan et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: The intrasubunit connections between the RCK1 site and Ca2+ bowl (R514-Y904/E902 interactions) are potential candidates for the structural determinants underlying a cooperative mechanism between the RCK1- and RCK2-sensor.
source: In fact, a recent functional study of the intrasubunit connections between the RCK1 site and Ca2+ bowl (R514-Y904/E902 interactions) has shown that such connections are potential candidates for the structural determinants underlying a cooperative mechanism between the RCK1- and RCK2-sensor.
evidence: Supported by citation to functional study.

claim: These interactions are involved in either the preservation of the integrity of RCK1 Ca2+-binding site or define the allosteric propagation pathway of the chemical energy induced by Ca2+ binding towards transmembrane domains.
source: These interactions are involved in either the preservation of the integrity of RCK1 Ca2+-binding site or define the allosteric propagation pathway of the chemical energy induced by Ca2+ binding towards transmembrane domains (Kshatri et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to functional study.

claim: There should be a positive cooperativity between the Ca2+-binding at RCK1 site and the Ca2+ bowl since the Ca2+-induced conformational change of the RCK1-N lobes from closed to open configuration depends on the functional state (unliganded and liganded) of both RCK sites.
source: On the basis of the cryo-EM structure of Aplysia californica BK channel, (Hite et al., 2017) proposed that there should be a positive cooperativity between the Ca2+-binding at RCK1 site and the Ca2+ bowl since the Ca2+-induced conformational change of the RCK1-N lobes from closed to open configuration depends on the functional state (unliganded and liganded) of both RCK sites.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on structural data.

claim: Functional studies point out a more relevant role of the intrasubunit cooperativity (albeit modest) than the intersubunit cooperativity between the RCK Ca2+ sites.
source: However, functional studies point out a more relevant role of the intrasubunit cooperativity (albeit modest) than the intersubunit cooperativity between the RCK Ca2+ sites (Niu and Magleby, 2002; Qian et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to functional studies.

claim: A concerted CTD-VSD model (Scheme II) gives better explanation than an independent CTD-VSD model (Scheme I) to the allosteric communication of the calcium and voltage sensors.
source: Thus, although a concerted CTD-VSD model (Scheme II) gives better explanation than an independent CTD-VSD model (Scheme I) to the allosteric communication of the calcium and voltage sensors, more work is required to explore improved models able to reproduce more accurately the properties of the interaction CTD-VSD mechanism in BK channel.
evidence: This is concluded from the model fitting and statistical analysis of experimental data.
